messages:
maya: hey folks, trying to accept the GitHub org invite but it errors with 'This invite cannot be accepted because this account has a conflicting email'. I have a personal GH account (maya.dev) and a work account invite sent to maya@redwood.ai. What do I do?

github-bot: If you have multiple GitHub accounts with the same email, you need to either add the work email to the account you intend to use, or the org admin can resend the invite to a different username. See https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/organizing-membership/managing-membership-in-your-organization/adding-people-to-your-organization.

maya: I definitely used my personal account for some OSS stuff (maya.dev). I tried adding maya@redwood.ai to maya.dev but GitHub says that email is already in use by another account: maya-work. I'm stuck in a loop.

sam-onboard: hey @maya, thanks for flagging. Two options: 1) we can reissue the invite to your personal username (maya.dev) and then enforce SSO, or 2) you can transfer ownership of the work email to one account. For speed, option 1 is easiest. Which GH handle do you want us to invite?

maya: I prefer keeping my OSS account separate. Please invite maya.dev. Also I want to continue using SSH keys from my laptop (same key across accounts). Will that be a problem?

rachel-security: SSH keys can be reused across accounts but it's better to add a new deploy key or a separate key per account for auditability. If you reuse the same key, security may flag it during an audit. If you want to reuse, go to https://github.com/settings/ssh/new and add the key to the invited account after acceptance.

tom-devex: @sam-onboard if you resend invite to maya.dev we'll also need to add them to teams: engineers, docs-contributors. I'll take care of team mapping once the invite is accepted.

sam-onboard: reissued invite to username: maya.dev (check email and your GitHub notifications) :white_check_mark:

maya: I got the invite, clicked Accept, then GitHub redirected me to the org SSO page which prompted me to Authorize. It then failed with 'You must enable two-factor authentication before joining this organization.' I already have 2FA on maya.dev via SMS (older phone).

rachel-security: org requires app-based 2FA (authenticator or security key). SMS-only is not allowed. Please set up an authenticator (or add a security key) under Settings -> Security -> Two-factor authentication. Steps: 1) Settings -> Security -> Enable two-factor authentication -> use an authenticator app. 2) Save recovery codes.

maya: switched to authenticator app and saved codes. Re-attempting accept now.

maya: accepted and authorized SSO, but I still can't clone private repos: `git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/console.git` returns `Permission denied (publickey)`.
tom-devex: run `ssh -vT git@github.com` and paste output (redact IPs). Also check `ssh-add -l` to ensure your key is loaded.
maya: output shows my key not loaded. I added it with `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_rsa` and now `ssh -T git@github.com` says 'Hi maya.dev! You've successfully authenticated'. Trying clone again... works!

sam-onboard: added maya.dev to teams: engineers, docs-contributors. You should also see repos now. Welcome :tada:

maya: thanks everyone. One last thing: the invite email to maya@redwood.ai still exists on the other work account (maya-work). Should I delete that email from maya-work to avoid confusion?
rachel-security: you can remove the work email from the unused account to prevent future conflicts, but if you ever need access to that account later keep it detached. If you want, we can also mark the other account as deprovisioned in our access tracker.
maya: please mark it deprovisioned.
sam-onboard: filed ACC-4180 to deprovision `maya-work` and remove maya@redwood.ai from that account. Closing this thread once deprovision is complete.
maya: resolved for me, thanks all :pray:
